definitions.definition: artificial intelligence system means a technological system that, autonomously or partly autonomously, processes data related to human activities through the use of a genetic algorithm, a neural network, machine learning or another technique in order to generate content or make decisions, recommendations or predictions.
definitions.locator: Artificial Intelligence and Data Act, section 2 (enacted by clause 39 of Bill C-27), page 98 (printed page 86)

definitions.definition: high-impact system means an artificial intelligence system that meets the criteria for a high-impact system that are established in regulations.
definitions.locator: Artificial Intelligence and Data Act, section 5(1) (enacted by clause 39 of Bill C-27), page 100 (printed page 88)

note: Quoted from the English text of Bill C-27 as printed at first reading on June 16, 2022 (official.pdf, a bilingual print with English and French in parallel columns; the text layer holds each page's text twice, once with margin line numbers, and the quotes are from the copy without them). Part 3 of the bill enacts the Artificial Intelligence and Data Act: section 2 defines 'artificial intelligence system' for the whole Act and section 5(1) defines 'high-impact system' for its Part 1. 'High-impact system' is the bill's own term and is grouped under high-risk AI system only for comparison; the definition leaves the criteria to regulations. The Act does not define 'artificial intelligence' on its own, or any model term, generative AI or general-purpose AI. 'Automated decision system' is defined in the bill, but in section 2(1) of the Consumer Privacy Protection Act enacted by Part 1 (page 15), not in the Artificial Intelligence and Data Act, so it is not counted for this record. The secondary file (secondary.html) is the LEGISinfo page of Bill C-27, which lists the bill's stages and does not contain its text.
